title: fix(pm): the scratch-dir scan does not read a declaration as a directory-creating site
body:
Fixes #23294
Clause-②: no

`main`'s hourly full battery is red on `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (the card behind it is #23274). The live-tree case "no mkdtempSync site in this tree takes a base the scan cannot read" reads `examples/app-showcase/types/node-shim.d.ts:30` as a call. That line is a type declaration, `export function mkdtempSync(prefix: string): string;`, and the scan cannot resolve its "base", `prefix: string`. The declaration is correct and the reader is wrong, so this PR fixes the reader. The shim is not touched, and no gate is added.

## The change

`scratchDirSitesInSource` (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`) no longer counts a declaration as a directory-creating site. It recognises two shapes:

- **A declaration file** (`.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, `.d.cts`). TypeScript admits no statement in an ambient context, so every match in one is a signature, and the function returns zero sites for it.
- **A match the `function` keyword precedes.** This covers `declare function`, `export function`, an overload, and the head of a same-file wrapper. What follows the name there is a parameter list being declared, not an argument being passed. `singleCallSiteParameters` already uses the same test to skip its own declarations.

Every other match is judged exactly as before. `SCRATCH_CALL`, the resolver and the verdict are unchanged. A wrapper's body is still read, because the calls inside it are calls.

**Deliberately narrow.** An interface method signature, an object-literal method or a class method in an ordinary `.ts` / `.mjs` source is still read as a site. The text that would clear one (a name, an argument list, then `:`) is also the text of a ternary's call, and this scan's bias is to report a site rather than clear it. A shape this rule does not clear fails loud, with its file and line. None of those shapes occurs in the tree today (measured below).

## What moved on the tree

A probe listed every raw `SCRATCH_CALL` match in the tracked JS/TS sources, with the module's own classification of each. "Before" is the base `bae5841bce` and "after" is the fix, measured both before and after the merge of `main` (the same numbers both times):

| | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| raw matches | 1764 | 1764 |
| sites the scan counts | 1764 | 1762 |
| in-tree sites | 63 | 63 |
| exposed | 0 | 0 |
| unresolved, all | 315 | 313 |
| unresolved `mkdtempSync` | 1 | 0 |

The in-tree, covered, exposed and unresolved lists from `exposedScratchDirs` were also diffed field by field between the base tree and the fix. They differ by two unresolved entries, both in the shim, and by nothing else:

- line 30, `mkdtempSync` with `prefix: string`, which is the red;
- line 26, `mkdirSync` with `path: string`, which has been there since `24964153e2`. It was silent only because the `mkdirSync` half is not held to completeness.

No in-tree, covered or outside site moved.

**Other declaration shapes.** Across all 1764 raw matches, 2 sit in a declaration file, and the same 2 are `function`-keyword declarations. Outside the shim, no match is followed by `:` or `{` after its argument list, and no match has a type-annotated first argument. So the tree has no `declare function`, overload, interface signature or method in a `.ts` source to handle today.

## Self-test: six new cases, in the fast tier

The six new cases are in-process fixtures, so they sit in the **fast tier**, which is the tier this PR's lane runs. Each rule is pinned on a fixture only it can clear, and three controls keep both rules honest:

1. A module shim's two signatures in a `.d.ts` are no site.
2. The file rule alone: an interface method signature in a `.d.mts`, with no `function` keyword, is no site.
3. The keyword rule alone: `declare function`, `export function` and an overload in a `.ts` source are no site.
4. CONTROL: `const dir = mkdtempSync(someUnreadableBase);` in a `.ts` source is still UNRESOLVED. The case asserts the call name and the expression.
5. CONTROL: the same call beside a declaration of the same name is still the one site, UNRESOLVED on line 2.
6. CONTROL: in a wrapper `function mkdirSync(dir)` whose body calls `fs.mkdirSync(dir, …)`, the head is not a site and the body's call is, UNRESOLVED on line 2.

The live-tree case is unchanged and stays in the slow tier.

**The battery, both tiers** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test`, the equivalent of the schedule and push runs):

- **Before**, at `bae5841bce`: `✗ dispatch-gates self-test: 1 of 2093 case(s) failed.`, exit 1. The one red is the card's case, word for word.
- **After**, at `82522ac6a8` (this PR's head): `✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 2099 cases pass.`, exit 0, with `fast 1839 case(s) in 428.5s · slow 260 case(s) in 1253.3s`. The live-tree cases now read:
  - `✓ the sweep really read this tree (1762 directory-creating site(s) across 8973 tracked source(s))`
  - `✓ and it really found in-tree fixture roots (63)`
  - `✓ no mkdtempSync site in this tree takes a base the scan cannot read`

The six-case difference is these cases: the tier-partition pin moved from `1817 fast + 260 slow` to `1823 fast + 260 slow`.

## Ablations (one-time proofs, nothing left in the tree)

Each mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, on `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, with the fast tier as the wrapped command. Every leg reported the anchor going from 1 to 0 and a changed blob hash. Every restore reported a blob equal to HEAD (`c7096603fe14`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. A driver script re-checked both after each leg, and the tree held zero ablation markers at the end.

| ablation | expected | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1: the declaration-file early return removed | case 2 red | **case 2 red, 1 of 1839**. It found the `.d.mts` signature as an UNRESOLVED site. |
| A2: the `function`-keyword skip removed | case 3 red | **cases 3, 5 and 6 red, 3 of 1839.** That is wider than I predicted, and correctly so: cases 5 and 6 assert that the declaration line is not a site, as well as that the call is one. |
| A3: the keyword test made to match everything, so every site is cleared | cases 4 to 6 red | **cases 4, 5 and 6 red, 3 of 1839**, each reading `scanned: 0` |

## Local verification, at `82522ac6a8`

- **Derived gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 29 commands, and all 29 exited 0. The reconciliation (`--ran`) reads: `29 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 29 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)`. `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` runs the wrapper self-test and then the dev-box fast tier. It exited 0 with 1839 fast cases.
- **Selected CI family outside the derived list.** The CI selector, run locally as a `pull_request` event, also selects `bare_root_worklist`, which is not among the 29. `node scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs --self-test` exited 0.
- **Lint, as a proven narrowing.**
  - Population: the two touched files. `eslint.config.mjs` lints both, and neither came back ignored.
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict for any untouched file.
  - The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- **`pnpm check:nul-bytes`:** OK, 11261 text files, no raw control bytes.

## Whether `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` runs on this PR

It does. `scripts/ci/select-gate-families.sh`, run locally as a `pull_request` event against this branch, prints `run   pm_dispatch_gates      reads scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs (M, scripts)`, because `scripts/pm/*` is in that family's read-set.

On `pull_request` and `merge_group`, though, the lane runs the **fast tier only**. So this PR's CI reads the six new cases, but **not** the live-tree case, which runs on `push` to `main` and on the hourly schedule. The both-tiers result above is the local equivalent of that run.

PR #23273's paths were outside the read-set: whole-tree content reads are off the PR path by a ruled narrowing. That is why only the hourly run caught the red.

## Changeset

None, with label `skip-changeset`. Both touched files belong to the repository root package, `@objectstack/spec-monorepo`, which is `"private": true` and declares no `files`, so nothing here is published. The nearest `package.json` above each file is the root's.

Positive control: the same lookup on `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` lands on `@objectstack/spec`. That package is not private, and its `files` list includes `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so that file does publish.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **`ci-failure.mjs --run` misses a roster member.** `node scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs --run 38411694784`, re-run for this PR, still exits 2. It says that `Lint & Repo Gates` has "NONE of its members … among this sha's check-runs". The red member is there: three check-runs named `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` exist on `042ef51530`, a success (run `38409754946`), the failure (`115345404875`, run `38411694784`) and a later cancelled one (`115345950501`, run `38411617233`). The likeliest reading, not verified in the code, is that grouping by name across every run on the sha keeps the later cancelled row, and that row is not in the asked run. This is out of this card's scope and is handed to the seat with the evidence above.
- **The fast tier and the in-process scratch cases.** The existing hermetic scratch-scan cases still sit inside the slow section "the change set derived from git", next to the git fixtures. They are in-process and could run in the fast tier too. They are left where they are, with a pointer to the new block. Carrier: none.
